title: CAP Theorem — Full JSON Block Demo
description: Interactive demo article using every engineering blog block type: video, code, polls, tables, and SEO fields. Learn CAP (Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance) for interviews and system design.
author: Pawan Bisht

blocks.title: Demo article
blocks.text: This page exercises every JSON block type supported by the engineering blog renderer — including video. Content is real; structure is the showcase.
In a distributed data store, when a network partition happens, you cannot simultaneously guarantee both perfect consistency and perfect availability — you choose a tradeoff.
Colored text block example for emphasis.

blocks.html: This is richText with inline HTML — use sparingly for trusted author content only.

columns.title: Consistency
columns.body: Every read receives the most recent write or an error.

columns.title: Availability
columns.body: Every request receives a non-error response.

columns.title: Partition tolerance
columns.body: System continues despite dropped or delayed messages between nodes.

items: Identify your failure domains (AZ, region, network).
Decide RPO/RTO with product and legal.
Choose CP vs AP per data path — not one global answer.

items.text: Expose consistency mode in API docs

blocks.text: It's not about choosing CAP — it's about choosing which guarantees matter for each operation.

blocks.title: Interview tip
blocks.text: Name the partition first, then explain which leg you relax and how clients detect stale reads.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Calling a single monolith 'CA' while ignoring that production always has partial failures.

blocks.title: Outage pattern
blocks.text: Split-brain writes without conflict resolution can corrupt financial balances.

blocks.title: PACELC
blocks.text: When the network is normal, you still trade latency vs consistency — CAP is the partition case of a broader design space.

blocks.question: For a checkout API during a partition, which default do you prefer?

items.title: Is CAP still relevant in 2026?
items.body: Yes as a framing tool. Modern systems add PACELC and per-operation consistency levels.

items.title: Does Redis choose AP or CP?
items.body: Depends on mode: single primary with sync replication leans CP; async replication allows availability with lag.
